sources:

- Edmunds 2025 Ariya: https://www.edmunds.com/nissan/ariya/2025/trims/

infotainment: Dual 12.3-inch displays (digital instrument cluster + center touchscreen) with NissanConnect with Google built-in; wireless Apple CarPlay; wired Android Auto
adasStandard: Nissan Safety Shield 360 standard: automatic emergency braking with pedestrian detection, blind-spot warning, rear cross-traffic alert, lane-departure warning, high-beam assist, rear automatic braking. ProPILOT Assist (adaptive cruise + lane-keeping) standard. Source: https://www.nissanusa.com/vehicles/electric-cars/ariya/features.html
adasOptional: ProPILOT Assist 2.0 (hands-off highway driving on mapped roads) available on higher trims with NissanConnect Services subscription. Source: https://www.nissanusa.com/experience-nissan/news-and-events/nissan-propilot-assist.html
rearViewCameraNotes: Standard rearview camera with dynamic guidelines. Higher trims add HD enhanced viewing and Intelligent Around View Monitor (360-degree surround). Source: https://www.nissanusa.com/vehicles/electric-cars/ariya/features.html
sideViewCameraNotes: Engage base trim lacks the 360-degree Around View Monitor system; standard side cameras are limited to blind-spot warning radar (no LaneWatch-style side camera).
subscriptionFeatures: NissanConnect Services: Select tier (~$199.95/yr after trial) for basic remote start/lock/locator; Premium tier (~$299.95/yr) adds destination assist, voice services; Premium+ (~$399.95/yr) adds in-car Wi-Fi. ProPILOT Assist 2.0 (where equipped) requires active NissanConnect Services Premium+ subscription. Source: https://www.nissanusa.com/connect.html
drmNotes: Vehicle operates fully offline. NissanConnect Services telematics features (remote start/lock, in-car Wi-Fi, real-time traffic, navigation updates) require subscription after included trial. ProPILOT Assist 2.0 hands-off mode requires active NissanConnect subscription to function — drops to ProPILOT Assist 1.0 (hands-on) when subscription lapses. Source: https://www.ariyaforums.com/threads/pro-pilot-assist-2-0-subscription-length.865/
killSwitchNotes: No federal impaired-driving-detection kill switch present in MY2025; the NHTSA IIJA mandate has not yet been finalized and not yet effective. Source: https://www.kbb.com/car-news/nhtsas-new-kill-switch-law-approaches-key-deadline/
knownIssues: Reported owner concerns: software glitches in early units, charging-port reliability issues, DC fast-charge tapering more aggressively than peers. Sources: https://recharged.com/articles/2025-nissan-ariya-problems ; https://recharged.com/articles/2025-nissan-ariya-reliability-rating
recalls: Data unavailable: searched NHTSA recall database via summary sources; no major MY2025-specific recall summaries surfaced. Refer to nhtsa.gov VIN-specific lookup at time of purchase.
stateIncentives: State-level incentives vary: CA Clean Vehicle Rebate Project (CVRP) currently waitlisted; CO offers up to $5,000 EV tax credit; NY Drive Clean Rebate up to $2,000. As of October 2025 federal IRA tax credits have ended. Source: https://fueleconomy.gov/feg/taxevb.shtml
tcoSource:
Primary: CarEdge Nissan ARIYA (https://caredge.com/nissan/ariya/costs) — 5-year total $56,314; depreciation $31,911 (from $50,381 new to ~$18,470 residual — heavy EV depreciation), insurance $12,670 ($2,534/yr), electricity $2,285 (95 MPGe, 15k mi/yr), financing $7,865 (72mo @ 6.99% APR, 20% down), maintenance+repairs $1,582 combined (split ~60/40 to $949 maintenance / $633 repairs).

5-year TCO compiled 2026-05-21. 15,000 mi/yr.

**Primary depreciation source (per-trim):** [KBB 2025 Nissan ARIYA Engage+ e-4ORCE](https://www.kbb.com/nissan/ariya/2025/engage_plus-e-4orce/) — KBB lists this trim but per-trim cost-to-own dollar breakdown was not directly extractable (KBB pages blocked via WebFetch 403). Depreciation interpolated linearly by MSRP between two anchor trims on the same model year:
- [KBB 2025 ARIYA Engage (FWD)](https://www.kbb.com/nissan/ariya/2025/engage/): 5-yr depreciation $26,987, residual $14,173, MSRP $41,160.
- [KBB 2025 ARIYA Evolve+ e-4ORCE](https://www.kbb.com/nissan/ariya/2025/evolve_plus-e-4orce/): 5-yr depreciation $33,065, residual $16,695, MSRP $48,370.
Interpolation position: (45,370 − 41,160) ÷ (48,370 − 41,160) = 0.584 → depreciation = $26,987 + 0.584 × ($33,065 − $26,987) = **$30,538**.

**Component cost model (model-level, applied per-trim):** [CarEdge Nissan ARIYA](https://caredge.com/nissan/ariya/costs) — 5-year baseline (avg new $50,381): insurance $12,670/5y ($2,534/yr), fuel $2,285/5y (95 MPGe avg), maintenance+repairs $1,582/5y (split 60/40 → $949 maintenance / $633 repairs per Edmunds methodology), financing $7,865/5y (72mo @ 6.99% APR, 20% down).

**Per-trim scaling:** Fuel held at $2,285 — Engage+ e-4ORCE rated 95 MPGe combined (matches CarEdge baseline). Insurance and financing scaled to this trim's MSRP+dest $46,760 → insurance $11,759; financing $7,300.

**Cross-references:** [Edmunds TCO model-level](https://www.edmunds.com/nissan/ariya/2025/cost-to-own/) — 2025 ARIYA model-level $62,994 total, $26,498 depreciation, $36,496 OOP. KBB family overview: [Nissan ARIYA 2025 Cost to Own](https://www.kbb.com/nissan/ariya/2025/cost-to-own/).

**Taxes & fees:** Not itemized by KBB or CarEdge for EV cost-to-own. Omitted rather than estimated.

tcoSource:
5-year TCO compiled 2026-05-21. 15,000 mi/yr. **MY2026 Nissan Rogue Plug-in Hybrid is the first Nissan PHEV in the U.S. market; no Nissan-published or aggregator-published per-trim cost-to-own exists yet.** Compiled by analog from the mechanically identical 2026 Mitsubishi Outlander PHEV (same platform, drivetrain, battery, EV range — Nissan SL premium ~$5,500 over Outlander per [Autoblog](https://www.autoblog.com/news/2026-nissan-rogue-phev-pricing)).

**Pricing anchor:** MSRP $45,990 + destination $1,545 = $47,535 ([Nissan press release](https://usa.nissannews.com/en-US/releases/2026-nissan-rogue-plug-in-hybrid-pricing-starts-at-45990)).

**Depreciation:** [iSeeCars Outlander PHEV resale value](https://www.iseecars.com/car/mitsubishi-outlander-phev/resale-value) — PHEV depreciates 52.7% over 5 years (faster than hybrid-compact-SUV avg 36.3%, reflecting steeper PHEV depreciation curve). Applied to $47,535 → 52.7% × $47,535 = $25,051. Cross-reference: [KBB 2025 Outlander (non-PHEV)](https://www.kbb.com/mitsubishi/outlander/2025/cost-to-own/) lists $21,252 over 5y on lower MSRP; PHEV adjustment per iSeeCars rate.

**Insurance:** [insuraviz 2025 Mitsubishi Outlander PHEV insurance](https://insuraviz.com/vehicles/mitsubishi/mitsubishi-outlander-phev-insurance/) — national avg $2,156/yr × 5 = $10,780.

**Fuel:** Mixed-mode PHEV at 15k mi/yr. Assume ~60% on electric (38-mi EV range, 7.5h L2 charge, suitable for typical daily commute) → 9,000 mi/yr electric at 34 kWh/100mi × $0.16/kWh = $490/yr = $2,448/5y. Remaining 40% gas at EPA 26 mpg combined hybrid mode → 6,000 mi/yr ÷ 26 × $3.50/gal = $808/yr = $4,038/5y. Total fuel/energy: **$6,486/5y**.

**Maintenance & repairs:** PHEV has ICE plus EV components — uses both gas-engine service and EV servicing windows. CarEdge gas Outlander ([costs](https://caredge.com/mitsubishi/outlander/costs)) reports $2,487 maintenance+repairs over 5y; PHEV slightly higher due to dual-system complexity. Estimate $2,800 combined, split 60/40 per Edmunds methodology → $1,680 maintenance, $1,120 repairs.

**Financing:** 72-month loan @ 6.99% APR, 20% down on $47,535 → $38,028 financed → ~$7,420 interest over 5 years (consistent with [CarEdge Outlander baseline](https://caredge.com/mitsubishi/outlander/costs) $6,042 on lower MSRP, scaled).

**Taxes & fees:** Not itemized; varies by state. Omitted rather than estimated.

**Edmunds/KBB-direct attempts:** [Edmunds 2026 Rogue PHEV](https://www.edmunds.com/nissan/rogue-plug-in-hybrid/) and [KBB 2026 Rogue PHEV](https://www.kbb.com/nissan/rogue-plug-in-hybrid/) cost-to-own pages exist but did not publish dollar breakdowns at compile time (WebFetch blocked 403; pages may carry 'Data Unavailable' for this first-year nameplate). Re-evaluate once 2026 model-year aggregator data matures.
